queue.label: Feedback queue
queue.sub: A triage queue pushed one item at a time — who owns it and what happens next are on this page.

tab.scopeHint: Status tabs filter only the page in hand; other pages may have more with this status

empty.title: No feedback yet
empty.desc: Nobody has submitted feedback yet. New submissions show up in this queue.

filtered.title: No feedback matches
filtered.desc: Try another keyword, or click "All" to clear the filters.

queueDetail.author: Submitted by
queueDetail.securityHint: Once marked as a security issue this item is hidden from your colleagues: only the submitter and you, an admin, can see it. Anyone else who opens it just sees that it cannot be opened.
queueDetail.notesHint: Only admins can see these, not the submitter. Once added a note stays put: it cannot be edited or deleted.
queueDetail.notePlaceholder: Write something for whoever picks this up next

filtered.title: No feedback matches
filtered.desc: Try another keyword, or click "All" to clear the filters.

cost.note: Priced at each model's rate in the gateway's price table; subscription calls are estimated at the same model's rate. Unpriced tokens have no rate and are not in that figure.

empty.title: No data yet
empty.desc: The platform hasn't produced any data yet.

perf.note: Latency per route, held in process memory: this moment only, cleared on restart, and this process only (the business API). A weekly view would have to read the request log instead.
perf.routesNote: Every registered endpoint gets a row, never-hit ones included (their call count shows an em-dash). The percentiles are exact over the last 256 samples, not lifetime.

network.title: Network throughput
network.uplinkNote: The default-route interface ({iface}). Uplink includes the metering proxy egress to model providers, repo sync and backups — this is the box total uplink, not just our users traffic. History is process memory and clears on restart.
network.apiNote: HTTP request-body bytes in and response-body bytes out of this backend process.

usage.byModelNote: Bar is tokens; the last two columns are money and unpriced tokens. All three together answer "is it the model or the billing".
usage.byRouteNote: The unpriced column is tokens with no rate; split by route, it shows which route they came from, and where the KPI's number comes from.

machines.title: Machines (stock)
machines.note: These four are stock counts from four ledgers, not live online counts — online state lives in process memory and has no column in the database.

column.title: By column
column.note: These four are filters, not a partition: "Agent-filed" is a source and overlaps public/private, so they don't sum to the total.

health.title: Platform health
health.note: This moment only — not stock, not a window. Same checks as /health/detailed.

spine.title: Delivery chain
spine.note: Four stations are throughput at different moments, not a funnel over one cohort. The merge station counts PR cards only — a card without a PR has pr_merged_at empty forever. The machine gate is retired and not on the chain (#296).

stuck.title: Stuck cards
stuck.note: Stuck is judged by note_code in the stuck set, never by note text — a code left out of the set is silent forever.

needs.title: Needs you
needs.note: Three reasons only — the closed set in delivery/addressing.py (reviewer / reporter / asked).

failures.title: Turn failures
failures.note: Structured source is blocks.meta code, not agent_turns — that table has no failure column. Credits refusals are counted separately via credits_refused_at.

host.title: Host failure streaks
host.empty: No hosts with a failure streak
host.note: Current streak only — any success deletes the row, so this cannot answer how many were quarantined last week.

backlog.note: Backlog is stock. A live card blocks the room from re-filing, so in-flight is not just queueing slowly.

product.northStarNote: Bucketed by decided_at. It is the LAST decision time and revoke overwrites it — a card accepted then revoked loses its accept moment.

rejection.title: Where filed cards ended
rejection.note: Returned = rejected + gate red/blocked + conflict + void. A true revoke is not a return. Denominator is cards filed in the window (including still-live).

unavailable.title: Not computable today
unavailable.note: No data source. Any number here would have to be invented.
unavailable.summon: Acceptance rate after summoning the agent: agent_turns has no summon flag and accept_cards has no origin turn — there is no foreign key between them.
unavailable.churn: Churn after credits exhausted: compute_grants has no exhausted_at, user has no last_login.

oauth.title: OAuth credentials
oauth.note: Missing refresh_token is not the same as expired: an expired one can still be refreshed, one without refresh is permanently dead on expiry. token_expires is a fixed expiry, not a recent failure.

passkey.title: Passkey coverage
passkey.note: Denominator is all non-deleted accounts, not active ones (user has no last_login). TOTP lives in Redis, not the database — so this reports passkey, not 2FA coverage.

delivery.title: Delivery ledger
delivery.note: Two tiers: the first is still retried, the second is abandoned after MAX_ATTEMPTS. Collapsing them makes salvageable and hopeless look alike.

unavailable.title: Not observable today
unavailable.note: Needs instrumentation. A zero here would mean checked and empty.
unavailable.githubAppPermissionGaps: GitHub App permission gaps: granted_permissions() lives 10 minutes in process memory and is never stored.
unavailable.githubAppMintFailureRate: GitHub App mint failure rate: logged only, never counted.
unavailable.loginLockoutStockAndRate: Login lockout history: login_security rate-limiters are Redis keys with no history.
unavailable.meteringPostFreeze: Metering posting freeze: admission fails open on transport errors and leaves no trace outside the log.

credits.title: Credits burnout
credits.note: Exhausted / low / unlimited are three mutually exclusive sets — unlimited is the ABSENCE of a grant. Burn rate is derived from resource_usage (compute_grants has no deduction ledger). ETA is linear extrapolation; unlimited and zero-burn both render —.

pool.title: Claude account pool
pool.note: Read from a snapshot the metering proxy writes beside the usage ledger (accounts.json), not from the database — the accounts behind the subscription route live only on the proxy's machine. The states are the proxy's own: cooling is a rate limit with a reset time, disabled has none and needs a manual reset. The snapshot ages, so when it is old it says when it was written.
pool.needsReset: the disabled ones need a manual reset

reason.notConfigured: This deployment has no subscription metering proxy, so the pool is not on the board
reason.missing: The metering proxy has not written a pool snapshot yet (it may not be running)
reason.unreadable: The pool snapshot could not be read
reason.malformed: The pool snapshot is not in a shape we can read
reason.unknown: The pool snapshot could not be read

disk.title: Disk (this backend)
disk.note: Covers only this host's workspace_root. Remote devices and cloud machines have their own disks and are invisible here.

preview.title: Preview tunnels
preview.note: Process memory, cleared on restart. This process only, not platform-wide.

machines.note: Rows and state distribution across four ledgers, not a container count — one-container-per-room has no transport yet.

hostSlots.title: Sandbox slots
hostSlots.note: Slots held by sessions / all slots across the host pool.

reliability.title: Delivery
reliability.note: Delivery backlog is stock, not a failure rate.

center.title: Feedback center

hot.note: Scored by support, but newer counts for more: 2 supports today weigh the same as 4 supports {halfLife} days ago. Items worth {threshold} points that aren't finished land in this tab; when fewer than {minItems} clear the bar the rest are filled in by score, so the tab is never empty.

center.foot: Public feedback is visible to everyone; if you file it as private, only you and platform admins can see it — nobody else can search it out or get a link to it.

empty.title: No feedback yet
empty.desc: Feedback you submit shows up here.

error.title: Couldn't load feedback
error.desc: Check your connection and try again.

filtered.title: No feedback matches
filtered.desc: Try another filter, or clear them to see everything.

search.title: No matching feedback
search.desc: Try another keyword. Search covers titles, summaries, bodies and submitters.

mine.title: My feedback
mine.lede: Feedback I filed, feedback I filed on behalf of an AI teammate, and feedback assigned to me.
mine.ledeRest: Other people's feedback isn't here — search for it in the feedback center.

empty.title: You haven't filed any feedback, and none is assigned to you

mine.foot: Finished feedback (fixed, shipped, won't fix) stays in the list but no longer accepts support; private items are visible only to you, platform admins, and the people who were in the channel where it was filed.

privateHint: Private feedback: only you, platform admins, and the people who were in the channel where it was filed can see it.
closedHint: Already closed — no need to support it

card.supportAria: Support this feedback, {n} supporters so far
card.unsupportAria: Remove your support, {n} supporters so far

comment.deleteAskWithReplies: Delete this comment and its {n} replies?

proposal.progress: You can follow its progress in the feedback center.
proposal.byline: {name} thinks this is a platform problem, not the way you're using it
proposal.userSaid: What you said at the time
proposal.why: Why (and why this isn't the way you're using it)
proposal.logsAttached: Attached ({n} characters); submitted along with the feedback

composer.placeholder: Add what you ran into, or why this change matters to you

aside.topic: Found in a conversation in a channel

delete.label: Delete
delete.askWithComments: Delete this report and its {n} comments?

missing.title: This feedback doesn't exist
missing.desc: It may have been deleted — or only the person who filed it, platform admins, and the people who were in the channel when it was filed can see it.

error.title: Couldn't load the details
error.desc: Check your connection and try again.

submit.title: Submit feedback

kind.label: What kind of feedback is this?

hint.suggestion: You want something to work better

submit.optionalDivider: Everything below is optional — write as much as you like. The more specific it is, the easier it is to reproduce and pick up.

placeholder.suggestion: What you would like improved, in one sentence
placeholder.other: What this is about, in one sentence

bug.label: What happened
bug.placeholder: What you did, and what actually happened

suggestion.label: What's not working well
suggestion.placeholder: How it is now, and how you'd like it to be

expectation.label: What you expected
expectation.placeholder: The result you expected from the same action

repro.label: How to reproduce
repro.placeholder: The shortest sequence from opening the page to seeing the problem

visibility.label: Who can see it

public.title: Public
public.hint: Visible to every signed-in user; can be supported and commented on

private.title: Private
private.hintWithRoom: Only you, platform admins, and the people who were in the channel where it was raised. It stays out of public lists and cannot be supported.
private.hintNoRoom: Only you and platform admins. It stays out of public lists and cannot be supported.

visibility.once: You decide this now, and only now — not even an admin has a way to make it public afterwards.

agent.title: From Cheese's investigation
agent.note: This feedback will be attributed to the AI teammate that found it, and you will be recorded as the submitter — both are kept, so "how much of what Cheese raised actually got filed" has an answer.
agent.attachHint: The context may contain your code snippets, file paths, or conversation text. With "Private", the people who can see it are you, platform admins, and the people who were in the channel where it was raised.
